findings.title: Include the identity type in denial-cache keys
findings.body: The denial key uses only the parsed UserUID, dropping IdentityType. Valid subjects anonymous:0 and render:0 therefore produce identical keys for the same namespace, action, name, and folder. If an anonymous request is denied access to a dashboard, a subsequent renderer check returns Allowed:false for 30 seconds, even though renderer permissions grant wildcard dashboard read access. Include the typed subject in the key so one identity's denial cannot block another.

findings.title: Avoid delimiter collisions between resource and parent names
findings.body: Joining unescaped components with underscores makes Name="a_b", ParentFolder="c" produce the same denial key as Name="a", ParentFolder="b_c" for the same namespace, user, and action. These inputs pass Check request validation. A denial for the first resource consequently denies access to the second for 30 seconds, even if the user has an explicit grant for it, because the denial cache is checked before permissions. Use an unambiguous encoding of the key components.

findings.title: Seed a granted permission in the denial-cache precedence test
findings.body: The "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" test seeds dashboards:uid:dash1 with false, despite intending to grant access. Without the denial-cache lookup, the cached permission check would still fail and the fake permission store would return no grants, so this test passes even if the new denial-cache fast path is removed. Set this permission to true so the test actually verifies that the denial entry takes precedence over a cached grant.
